items.title: Chow lemma for separated finite-type morphisms over a Noetherian base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: a04446e57ec1fbc252a871afcec7752fb2807b14
items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a quasi-projective proper modification of a separated finite-type scheme over a Noetherian base using closures of diagonal graph maps. Scheme-theoretic density permits gluing the local projections and proves exact inverse-image identities; these verify properness, surjectivity and a dense-open isomorphism. This is a substantive geometric construction beyond routine qualifying algebra.

items.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a refined weight filtration adapted to the braided product and derives ordered polynormal relations from the R-matrix. The mixed tensor factors require a second coadjoint-weight grading to eliminate unwanted leading terms; canonical-basis integrality then carries the construction over the Laurent ring. This is a substantive quantum-algebra structure proof rather than a direct use of Noetherianity for a commutative polynomial ring.

items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a cubic section through the maximal isotropic filtration of the pulled-back rank-two spectral bundle. items.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs a noise from the spatial product system and amplifies it without changing that system. It then chooses a unitary identification carrying the original dilation isometry to the noise isometry, transports the cocycle conjugacy, and checks the conditional-expectation identity using the increasing corner projection. items.difficulty_reason: The proof uses the canonical positive spinor bundle to replace the almost-complex section component by a circle quotient of sphere-bundle sections. It computes the rationalized section space, uses the nonzero Chern number to force the degree-one transgression, and eliminates the resulting acyclic generator pair from a Sullivan model. This ties spinorial geometry to the fundamental group and the full rational homotopy model of a function-space component; the base manifold itself need not be nilpotent.

The fibration4.1 and the generator elimination are explicit author constructions. Prior section-space rationalization, Thom mapping-space calculation and Crabb–Sutherland fundamental-group theorem are identified background. items.difficulty_reason: The new obligation is injectivity at the unbounded-cycle level: lifting a bounded homotopy alone does not connect its endpoints to the original unbounded operators. The author regularizes and doubles the operators, constructs an explicit rotated homotopy for cycles sharing a phase, and verifies its domain, compactness and graded-commutator requirements. This closes a nontrivial unbounded KK-theory equivalence and requires substantially more than a standard bounded functional-calculus exercise.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem5: integers g>L>=0, n>=1, nonnegative ordered d_i with sum d_i=3g-3+n and, for n>=3, sum of first n-2 d_i<=L; n=1,2 use the explicit unrestricted Pi_L conventions. original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly Theorem1.6 for every real nu>-1. items.difficulty_reason: Standard Day convolution, Gabriel localisation and pure-injective representability do not by themselves identify the maximal localising tensor ideals needed for this support. The author establishes the unique maximal localising tensor ideal extending a given maximal Serre ideal, using the internal-Hom kernel of its pure-injective residue weak ring and injective-hull comparisons across quotients. items.difficulty_reason: Classical dispersive norms are poorly behaved under the Moyal product, so standard small-data NLS scattering cannot be applied without constructing another analytic framework. items.difficulty_reason: The reverse Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives only one direction of the distance formula; obtaining the infimum requires global functions approximating a prescribed pair of points while satisfying a timelike bound everywhere. items.difficulty_reason: Ordinary trace cyclicity does not survive finite-part regularization: commutators create higher residue defects. items.difficulty_reason: The reflected vertex carries a truncated-polynomial nilpotent module, so the usual kernel/cokernel reflection for ordinary quivers does not provide the required map. items.title: The Sklyanin determinant of the complex reflection algebra B(n,l), for n at least two and zero at most l at most n, has the explicit ordered matrix-entry formula indexed by increasing tuples and image-supported permutations
items.author: Natasha Rozhkovskaya
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 6 (2010) article 100, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2010.100; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: A noncommutative reflection determinant cannot be expanded by the ordinary permutation rule because its shifted generating matrices are interleaved with R-matrices. The author reduces the antisymmetrized R-products to Jucys-Murphy sums, constructs a bijection reorganizing their transposition indices, and tracks the ordered matrix entries through repeated-image cycles. The surviving image-supported permutations and rational weights then give the explicit formula without commuting the algebra coefficients.

items.difficulty_reason: The authored proof translates failure of a bounded-round disjoint-disjunction search into consistency of a nonstandard universal-arithmetic theory via KPT witnessing. It constructs a formula with no proof in any standard propositional proof system and uses a two-stage model extension preserving Sigma-b-one properties and lengths to force a short proof and a falsifying assignment into the same sound model. Both student-teacher hardness and the open Problem2.2 model-extension hypothesis are indispensable explicit conditions; the claimed conclusion is a conditional complexity separation, not an unconditional solution to NP versus coNP.
